past.date: Tue 28 Jul 2026, before the US open
past.vs: Comparable EPS $0.97 vs $0.93 expected (+4%, Yahoo consensus), +11% vs a year earlier. Revenue $13.38bn vs about $13.17bn expected; +7% reported, +6% organic.
past.guide: 2026 organic revenue raised to about +5% (from 4-5%); comparable EPS growth raised to 9-10% (from 8-9%), including about a 3-point currency tailwind. Free cash flow about $12.4bn.
past.reaction: +5.0% on the day (close to close); +6.5% for the week vs +1.0% for the S&P 500.
take: Volume surge. Unit case volume +5% vs a year earlier; Coca-Cola credits its global FIFA World Cup campaign with part of the gain (the tournament ran 11 Jun-19 Jul, so it also helps Q3). Price/mix +2%; concentrate sales +4%.
Every region grew. Volume: Asia Pacific +8%, Bottling Investments +5%, EMEA +4%, Latin America +3%, North America +3%.
Margins up. Operating margin 34.9% vs 34.1% a year earlier; comparable 35.6% vs 34.7%.

Acquisitions and divestitures (including the CCBA sale, a 75% stake to Coca-Cola HBC, expected to complete by end-2026) take 2-3 points off 2026 reported revenue growth and about 1 point off EPS growth (Coca-Cola's 2026 guidance).
Calendar shift: Q4 2026 has six fewer days than Q4 2025, so reported Q4 growth will look weak.
past.impact: DM4a (organic +6%) and DM4b (volume +5%) both bullish; the World Cup boost will not repeat.

chains.name: Health rules on sugary drinks
path: SNAP soda bans, sugar taxes, GLP-1 drugs
evidence: At least 23 US states have approval to bar SNAP (food-stamp) money for soda; about 10 started in H1 2026 and about 20 by year-end. In the first 10, sugary-drink purchases by SNAP households fell 12% in H1 2026, and they did not switch to paying cash (Stanford/MIT/Chicago study, via Grocery Dive, 2 Sep 2026).
Numerator puts 2026 lost soda sales at up to $430m (29 May 2026), small vs Coca-Cola's $47.9bn revenue in 2025.
Mexico raised its tax on sugary drinks from Jan 2026; Coca-Cola FEMSA cited it for slightly lower Mexican volumes in H1 2026 (27 Jul 2026).
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs: outside estimates put about 12% of US adults on them, a drag of roughly 0.2% a year on US food and drink volume (OC&C, 2026).

When SEC works again, stage B must read Coca-Cola's revenue under the tag 'Revenues' (it does not use the default revenue tag).

DM1 compares reported revenue growth, which bottler sales cut: acquisitions and divestitures (including CCBA) take 2-3 points off 2026 reported revenue growth (Coca-Cola guidance). DM4a (organic growth) carries the clean demand read (Kenneth, 5 Oct 2026).

DM4a (organic revenue growth) is +6.0% in the June quarter, exactly on its +6% bullish line: at +5.9% it would score neutral and the composite would fall to about +20. 'What would change the call' does not yet list DM4 and DM5 (engine).
DM5 (bottler volumes) is shown as a leading read, but the bottlers report a few days after Coca-Cola, so it confirms rather than leads.

DM4a, DM4b and DM5 are entered from results releases, so they update quarterly. DM5 averages three bottlers whose bases differ slightly (CCEP days-adjusted, Coca-Cola HBC underlying, Coca-Cola FEMSA reported).
Q2 2026 volume (+5%) was helped by the global FIFA World Cup campaign (11 Jun-19 Jul) and good weather in Europe; the boost fades from Q4 2026.

Free cash flow in the quality check is $12.6bn for the last 12 months to Mar 2026 (SEC), but the 2025 quarters include a one-off $6.1bn payment to fairlife's former owners in Q1 2025. Coca-Cola guides about $12.4bn for 2026. The quality check shows 1 flag of 5: cash conversion (operating cash ÷ net profit) of 64% and 57% over the last two years, below the 70% line.

Revenue mix: Asia Pacific (about 12% of revenue) sits in Other with corporate and the removal of sales between segments, because its filing tag changed between filings. Costa and innocent moved into EMEA from 1 Jan 2025 (2024 restated), so EMEA's 3-year comparison is not like-for-like, and the Dec 2023 quarter is wrong (EMEA about $4.45bn, Other negative): its fourth quarter is worked out from a restated full year minus quarters on the old basis. Open item for the Framework chat.
Institutional change (LQ3) counts changes in existing positions only.
Short interest (LQ2) is only 0.9% of freely traded shares, below the 2% minimum, so it scores neutral.

Not scored but material: Coca-Cola's US tax case (transfer pricing; about $20bn exposure, $6bn already deposited) awaits an appeals court ruling after the 25 Jun 2026 hearing; and the Costa coffee sale was shelved in Jan 2026, with a possible write-down.

Peer set (Kenneth, 5 Oct: brand owners only): Mondelez's 31% gross margin is closer to the bottlers that were excluded than to Coca-Cola's 62%. Without Mondelez, VL1 would read neutral (24.7x vs a 20.8x median, +19%) and the composite would be about +34 (6 Oct estimate), above the Buy line (+30). The zone is sensitive to this choice.

shift.title: Coca-Cola is turning back into a pure concentrate business
pos: Bottling Investments fell from 17.6% to 12.0% of revenue in 3 years. The engine puts the margin gain from the change in mix at 3.1 points vs 3 years earlier, but much of that is an accounting artefact: Costa and innocent moved into EMEA from 1 Jan 2025 (2024 restated), which inflates EMEA's share. The gain from the bottler sales alone is smaller and not separately measured here.
The highest-margin regions (Latin America 60.4%, EMEA 37.5%) are growing at least as fast as the company (+6.5%, last 4 quarters vs the 4 before).
neg: Reported revenue shrinks with each bottler sale, so headline growth looks slower than the business: acquisitions and divestitures take 2-3 points off 2026 reported revenue growth (Coca-Cola guidance).
North America's reported margin dip (29.5% to 26.4%) is a one-off write-down, not a trend; excluding it the margin rose.
